objective_for_doctor: A 41-year-old Male patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have a cough, is your nose or the back of your throat itchy, and nasal congestion or a clear runny nose.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
Hi doctor. I’ve had a cough, and my nose and the back of my throat feel itchy. I also have nasal congestion with a clear runny nose.

Dr. Agent: I’m going to narrow this down—do you have fever, shortness of breath, or wheezing?  
Dr. Agent: How long has the cough and runny/itchy nose been going on, and do you have known seasonal allergies or eye itching/watery eyes?

I don’t have fever, and I’m not short of breath or wheezing. The cough and the runny/itchy nose have been going on for about a few days. I do have allergies—my family has a history of allergies/hay fever/eczema, and I’m more likely to have allergies, but I don’t remember having itchy/watery eyes specifically.
Doctor: Any sore throat, sneezing, or symptoms worse at night or with exposure to dust/pollen? Also, is the cough dry or productive (and if productive, what color)?
I don’t have a sore throat. I do have itchy nose and throat, and the cough is mostly dry. It seems a bit worse when I’m around dust or pollen, and it’s not really productive.

Doctor: Do you have any known asthma or prior episodes of similar symptoms, and are you experiencing trouble swallowing, facial pain/pressure, or headaches (more suggestive of sinus infection)?  
Doctor: Also—have you tried any antihistamine (like cetirizine/loratadine) or a nasal steroid spray, and did it help?

I don’t have asthma myself, but my family has asthma. I’m not having trouble swallowing, and I don’t really have facial pain/pressure or headaches. I haven’t tried cetirizine/loratadine or a nasal steroid spray yet.

Doctor: This pattern sounds most like an allergic rhinitis/post-nasal drip causing a dry cough—can you tell me: do you have sneezing or watery/itchy eyes, and is your cough worse when you lie down?  
Doctor: Also, any symptoms of COVID/flu (significant body aches, chills) or recent sick contacts?

I do have itchy nose and throat, and I’ve been coughing more when I lie down. I don’t know about sneezing or watery/itchy eyes—I haven’t really noticed them. I don’t have body aches or chills, and I don’t know of any recent sick contacts.

Doctor: Given the itchy nose/throat, clear runny nose, and cough that’s worse when you lie down, this strongly suggests allergic rhinitis with post-nasal drip rather than flu/COVID—any red flags like high fever, chest pain, or coughing up blood?  
Doctor: To confirm and guide treatment, do you have any history of asthma symptoms (prior wheeze or nighttime chest tightness), and would you agree to try an antihistamine and saline/nasal steroid next?

No red flags—I don’t have a high fever, chest pain, or coughing up blood. I haven’t had wheezing or nighttime chest tightness myself, and yes, I’m okay trying an antihistamine and saline/nasal steroid next.

Doctor: Sounds consistent with allergic rhinitis with post-nasal drip—do you have any thick yellow/green nasal discharge or bad tooth pain (to rule sinus infection), and would you like me to recommend a trial of cetirizine/loratadine plus saline rinse and an intranasal steroid?  
Doctor: I don’t think you need antibiotics or chest imaging right now given your few-day course, itchy eyes/throat/nose, clear runny drainage, and dry cough worse when lying down—DIAGNOSIS READY: Allergic rhinitis with post-nasal drip (upper-airway cough syndrome)
